mcp --agent <claude-code,cursor,codex>` with `--global` or `--project` writes a `bright-data` server entry, with the API key in plain text, into that agent's config. Without a TTY, pass `--agent`, plus `--global` or `--project` for Claude Code or Cursor.

In CLI 0.4.1 only Claude Code `--global` (`~/.claude.json`) and Cursor `--global` or `--project` (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`) land where the agent reads them. Claude Code `--project` writes `.claude/settings.json`, which Claude Code does not read for servers (it reads `.mcp.json`; the `brightdata-mcp` skill's references/setup.md has that block). For Codex, show the user this table and let them add it with their key:

[mcp_servers.bright-data]

findings.code_snippet:
## Where the key comes from

Highest first: the `--api-key` flag, then `BRIGHTDATA_API_KEY`, then `credentials.json` in the CLI's config directory. The paths per OS and what each refused call means are in the agent-onboarding skill's references/auth.md. Never print the key.

Running `login` again on a machine that already works replaces the stored key, so run `bdata zones --json` first and skip the login when it succeeds.

findings.code_snippet:
## A key from agent registration

An account created through agent registration has its own zones (`agent_unlocker`, `agent_serp`, `agent_browser_api`), and its key cannot create zones. The CLI's zone defaults use `cli_` names (`bdata login` sets `default_zone_unlocker` to `cli_unlocker`), which that account does not have, so `scrape` and `search` fail until the defaults point at the account's own zones:

```
bdata config set default_zone_unlocker agent_unlocker

findings.code_snippet:
Script paths in this file are relative to the scrape skill's folder.

The live catalogue is `GET https://api.brightdata.com/datasets/v3/scrapers`. It lists only real scrapers, 1006 of them on 2026-09-06, each with its variants: typed inputs and a control-panel link on every variant, output descriptions and a sample input on most (every bundled row has one). It needs the API key header. Without it the call returns 401, even though it is a free read. It takes exactly two filters: `?dataset_id=` returns one row and `?domain=` returns every scraper whose domain is exactly that string. | 1. Check what exists | `bdata zones --json` and read the names and types |
| 2. Point the config at a zone that exists | `bdata config set default_zone_serp <zone>`, using a real unlocker zone from your own `bdata zones --json` output, usually `cli_unlocker` |
| Cleaner alternative to step 2 | create a dedicated serp-type zone with `POST https://api.brightdata.com/zone`, Bearer auth, body `{"zone":{"name":"serp_live","type":"serp"},"plan":{"type":"unblocker","serp":true}}`, then `bdata config set default_zone_serp serp_live` |
| Either way | `--zone` on the call beats the config, so passing it explicitly fixes a single call without touching config |

In that body `plan.type` must be `unblocker` with `serp` set to true. There is no `serp` plan type.
